question: For several months, peaceful activists have been sitting in trees in the French department of Tarn to impede progress on the A69 motorway project. The information we have to hand indicates that the police response is a very serious overreaction.

Michel Forst, the UN Special Rapporteur on Environmental Defenders, has condemned actions taken by the police, such as depriving protestors of sleep by setting up floodlights at the edge of the forest, and depriving them of food and drinking water. Mr Forst also reports that the police stopped journalists from doing their job by side-lining them far from the protests. In light of the above: 1.

Is the Commission of the opinion that France has infringed the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, particularly Articles 1, 3 and 4 on human dignity, and Article 11 on the freedom of expression and information? 2. What steps will the Commission take to ensure that France upholds the fundamental rights enshrined in the Charter?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.5.2024) The Commission is committed to ensuring the respect of all fundamental rights enshrined in the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU (Charter) within the remit of its competences, including the right to freedom of expression and to peaceful assembly and association under respectively Articles 11 and 12 of the Charter.

In line with its Article 51(1), Charter applies to Member States only when they are implementing EU law. As set out in the Commission’s reply to written questions E-000243/2024 and E001428/2023, the definition and application of rules governing the holding of demonstrations, and the sanctions for not respecting them, are the Member States’ primary responsibility1.

In such cases, it is, in principle, for Member States, including their law enforcement and judicial authorities, to ensure that fundamental rights – including the freedom to receive and impart information without interference by public authority – are effectively respected and protected, in accordance with their national legislation and international human rights obligations.

Finally, the revised Environmental Crime Directive aims to strengthen the protection of environmental defenders in criminal proceedings by granting access to support and assistance measures in criminal proceedings in Member States, in accordance with national law.
1 Article 72 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union states that the constitution of an area of

freedom, security and justice ‘shall not affect the exercise of the responsibilities incumbent upon Member States with regard to the maintenance of law and order and the safeguarding of internal security’.
